bull.b: Term-based subscriptions create recurring revenue and give Zscaler a durable foundation for customer retention and expansion. Cross-selling products, modules, users and geographies can increase account value over time, supporting more predictable growth than one-time software sales.

Rapid growth alongside expanding large-enterprise adoption indicates that Zscaler is gaining strategic importance within customer security environments. Larger deployments can deepen switching costs, increase platform penetration and provide a durable base for future upsell opportunities.

Strong cash conversion and high gross margins provide resources to fund product development, infrastructure and go-to-market investment. Improving operating margins also demonstrate progress toward scalable economics, even as Zscaler continues expanding its cloud security platform.

bear.b: Persistent GAAP losses mean Zscaler has not yet converted its substantial revenue scale into consistent bottom-line profitability. Continued execution is required to translate positive EBITDA and cash flow into durable earnings while maintaining investment in growth and security innovation.

The lower forward growth outlook indicates that the exceptional expansion rate delivered in fiscal 2026 may not persist. Slower growth can reduce operating leverage, increase pressure on sales execution and make continued platform expansion more dependent on successful new products and larger deployments.

Higher spending on memory, storage, processors and infrastructure can absorb a larger share of revenue as Zscaler scales its platform. Sustained investment may constrain free cash flow margins and delay the conversion of improving operating performance into stronger long-term cash returns.
